components.responsibility: Invoke the documented API and retain returned outcomes.

components.label: Report API
components.responsibility: Authenticate a user, validate parameters and generate a bounded report within one request lifecycle.

components.label: Access check
components.responsibility: Validate principal and ownership before processing or returning an existing request receipt.

components.label: Request receipt store
components.responsibility: Bind owner/requestKey to a parameter hash and report ID atomically; identical retries share a receipt.

components.label: Source snapshot reader
components.responsibility: Choose an explicit read snapshot/cutoff and retain that input identity in report metadata.

components.label: Bounded renderer
components.responsibility: Enforce row, byte and work budgets; abort with explicit failure before publishing an incomplete artifact.

components.label: Immutable artifact store
components.responsibility: Store bytes under hash-addressed identity and bind output hash to the report; repeated identical writes are harmless.

components.label: Completion commit
components.responsibility: Commit metadata referencing an already written artifact; if commit fails keep a retriable/uncertain receipt and reconcile orphan bytes explicitly.

components.label: Failure and load observations
components.responsibility: For this hypothetical design record request duration, timeouts, CPU work and database wait as proposed measurements. A tenfold input is a scenario, not observed capacity.

components.label: Illustrative report user
components.responsibility: Invoke the documented API and retain returned outcomes.

components.label: Job submission API
components.responsibility: Persist a report job and dispatch intent atomically, return accepted, and let a leased worker publish completion later.

components.label: Job and request ledger
components.responsibility: Atomically create unique owner/requestKey receipt, parameter hash and job record; conflicting payloads reject.

components.label: Transactional dispatch outbox
components.responsibility: Commit outbox row with the job in the same database transaction; a dispatcher retries delivery by job ID.

components.label: Fenced worker claim
components.responsibility: Claim job with monotonically increasing fencing token and lease; completion verifies current token.

components.label: Snapshot report worker
components.responsibility: Pin query cutoff and renderer version in the job before work; retries reuse them or explicitly create a new report version.

components.label: Immutable output repository
components.responsibility: Write immutable content by hash; completion records one authorized artifact choice under the current fencing token.

components.label: Versioned status API
components.responsibility: Authorize each read and report accepted/running/complete/failed/uncertain; complete requires verified artifact and fenced metadata commit.

components.label: Lease and artifact reconciler
components.responsibility: Scan unfinished jobs and artifacts, verify identity/hash, requeue or reconcile with a fresh lease. Unknown irreversible effects stay uncertain.

requirements.text: Trace a specific report request through named state owners and separate accepted intent from completed output.
Explain a hypothetical failure and observable recovery without presenting it as an actual incident.
Compare structural choices at an illustrative tenfold workload and identify evidence needed to choose, without invented throughput results.

problem.scope: Explicitly illustrative worked examples, not the user's project, employment history or a claimed incident. Review a hypothetical report-generation product as two alternative designs: synchronous transactional requests and asynchronous durable jobs. All traffic, failures and scaling questions below are authored scenarios. Replace them with verified project facts before using as personal experience; no actual operated scale or business outcome is asserted.

solutions.chooseWhen: Reports may exceed a request deadline and explicit polling/notifications are acceptable.

invariants: An accepted response means durable intent, not a generated artifact.
stages.question: What can the initial response promise?
stages.reason: Persist a report job and dispatch intent atomically, return accepted, and let a leased worker publish completion later.
stages.title: Expose Job submission API

stages.question: Can a timeout submit duplicate jobs?
stages.reason: Atomically create unique owner/requestKey receipt, parameter hash and job record; conflicting payloads reject.
stages.title: Commit one job identity

invariants: No accepted job exists without durable dispatch intent.
stages.question: What if enqueue fails after job commit?
stages.reason: Commit outbox row with the job in the same database transaction; a dispatcher retries delivery by job ID.
stages.title: Avoid lost dispatch

invariants: Lease expiry alone never authorizes a stale token to commit.
stages.question: Can an expired worker publish stale completion?
stages.reason: Claim job with monotonically increasing fencing token and lease; completion verifies current token.
stages.title: Recover worker loss

invariants: One job ID does not silently change input semantics.
stages.question: Does a retry read different source data?
stages.reason: Pin query cutoff and renderer version in the job before work; retries reuse them or explicitly create a new report version.
stages.title: Compute from pinned inputs

invariants: Remote writes may duplicate, but stale workers cannot replace committed metadata.
stages.question: What if duplicate workers render the same job?
stages.reason: Write immutable content by hash; completion records one authorized artifact choice under the current fencing token.
stages.title: Store complete artifacts

invariants: Progress percentages, if used, are measured work or omitted.
stages.question: Can polling report complete before bytes exist?
stages.reason: Authorize each read and report accepted/running/complete/failed/uncertain; complete requires verified artifact and fenced metadata commit.
stages.title: Expose progress honestly

invariants: Recovery does not claim an incident actually occurred or prove deployed reliability.
stages.question: What if the worker dies between object write and completion?
stages.reason: Scan unfinished jobs and artifacts, verify identity/hash, requeue or reconcile with a fresh lease. Unknown irreversible effects stay uncertain.
stages.title: Resolve hypothetical interruptions

solutions.title: Illustrative asynchronous durable report jobs
tradeoffs: Job leases, recovery and versioned status add complexity.
Accepted is not complete; asynchronous dispatch alone establishes neither scale nor exactly-once external effects.
